correctness.rationale: For all n>=2 the plane-partition incidence rule identifies the induced boundary of an n-simplex. The cited two-toggle matching is acyclic, pairs only within or outside that core, and has no critical cells outside; hence there is a simplicial collapse onto the core. The half-turn is an exact permutation of core vertices, yielding degree (-1)^(n(n+1)/2) on integral top homology and the quotient rational homology by finite-group transfer. The bundled checker independently enumerates finite n=2,3,4 instances and full acyclicity at n=2,3.

value.rationale: The family-wide result provides a canonical half-turn invariant minimal sphere spine, an exact integral orientation character and the mod-four quotient rational homology dichotomy. It refines known nonequivariant homotopy information rather than recomputing the sphere count; its naturally defined symmetry action is not determined by ordinary Betti numbers.
